title: Mustache.jl
text: Documentation for Mustache.jl.

title: Examples
The pipeline
text: A template is specified and rendered with values coming from a view. This section gives some more detail.

title: Rendering
text: The render function combines tokens and a view to fill in the template. The basic call is render([io::IO], tokens, view), however there are variants: render(tokens; view...)render(tokens; kwargs...) Or (wherestring is parsed into tokens before rendering): render(string, view)render(string; …

title: Views
text: Views are used to hold values for the templates variables. title: Multiple views
text:
Support for more than one view is also provided. A simple example with two named tuples is: tpl = mt"""{{:a}} {{:b}} {{:c}}"""

title: Templates and tokens
text:

title: Tags
text: A template use tags to specify areas to be filled in by a view. There are numerous tag types, summarized in a table near the end of this document.

title: Variables
text: Tags representing variables for substitution have the form {{varname}}, {{:symbol}}, or their triple-braced versions {{{varname}}} or {{{:symbol}}}. The varname version will match variables in a view such as a dictionary or a module. The :symbol version will match variables passed in via named …

title: Filtering
text: This isn't part of the Mustache spec, but a filter can be applied to the value after it is looked up and before it is rendered. title: Sections
Using a true(ish) value to conditionally display a section
text:
When the variable is not a function or a container the part between them is used only if the variable is defined and not "falsy:" a = mt"{{#:b}}Hi{{/:b}}";
a(; b=true)  # "Hi"
a(; c=true)  # ""
a(; b=false) # "" also, as `b` is "falsy" (e.g., false, nothing, "")""  The Mustache spec call itself …

title: Inverted section tags
text: Related, if the tag begins with ^varname and ends with /varname the text between these tags is included only if the variable is not defined or is falsy. text: If the variable name refers to a function that function will be passed the unevaluated string within the section, as expected by the Mustache specification: Mustache.render("{{#:a}}one{{/:a}}", a=length)  # "3""3"  The specification has been widened to accept functions of two arguments, the string …

title: Iteration in a section
text: If the section variable, {{#varname}}, binds to an iterable collection, then the text in the section is repeated for each item in the collection with the view used for the context of the template given by the item. title: Mustache.load
text: Tuple{AbstractString, Vararg{Any}} Mustache.load(filepath, args...) Load file specified through  filepath and return the compiled tokens. Tokens are memoized for efficiency, Additional arguments are passed to Mustache.parse (for adjusting the tags).

title: Mustache.render_from_file
text:
Tuple{AbstractString, Any} render_from_file(filepath, view)
render_from_file(filepath; kwargs...) Renders a template from filepath and view. This function simply combines Mustache.render and Mustache.load and may be deprecated in the future.

title: Mustache.@jmt_str
text:
Tuple{String} jmt"string" String macro that interpolates values escaped by dollar signs, then parses strings. Note: very lightly modified from a macro in HypertextLiteral. Example: x = 1
toks = jmt"$(2x) by {{:a}}"
toks(; a=2) # "2 by 2"
